The Supreme Court on Wednesday ruled that the provision of the public offices election law denying voting rights to prisoners is constitutional, its first judgment on the matter.
The top court ruled that the restriction cannot be said to be unconstitutional at this stage.
Nine of the 15 justices of the court’s Grand Bench ruled the restriction constitutional, while the remaining six said it was unconstitutional or invalid. Six of the nine justices who upheld the restriction also called on the Diet, Japan’s parliament, to examine the issue further, citing insufficient public debate.
The law does not recognize the right to vote for individuals sentenced to imprisonment or a more severe penalty and still serving their sentences.
According to lower court rulings, the plaintiff, Kentaro Yagihashi, 40, was sentenced to seven years in prison for fraud in 2019. Due to the law, he was unable to vote in the 2021 House of Representatives election and other polls.
He subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking confirmation of his right to vote, as well as state compensation. Tokyo District Court dismissed his claims in 2023, finding the voting restriction to be constitutional. Tokyo High Court upheld the ruling in 2024, and the Supreme Court reached the same conclusion on Wednesday.

Yesterday, the Trump administration extended the reach of its existing export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips, namely, but not limited to, Nvidia's Blackwell lineup. The updated regulation now requires licenses for renting those chips in large quantities to the entirety of America's D:5 countries list (nations embargoed from arms sales). As expected, the news landed in Beijing like a lead dragon, and its Ministry of Commerce states that China "will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests." Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained The bold move taken by the U.S. arrives at a peculiar time, as President Trump is currently visiting the nation for the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Trump is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Nov. 19, a tête-a-tête that's bound to be interesting. Both nations were recently embroiled in a bitter trade war, with ever-mounting tariffs and restrictions on both sides until a temporary truce was called in Oct. 2025. Only some restrictions were lifted, though; for example, Chinese semiconductors still face a 50% tariff when imported stateside. A potential restart of tariff-slapping would all but guarantee an even larger amount of turmoil in U.S. stock markets. Those seas are already choppy enough thanks to Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang's romantic involvement with purported Chinese spy Alice Huang — along with mounting suspicions that the soulmates may have connived to siphon billions' worth of Blackwell chips from her Singaporean outfit Megaspeed onto Chinese AI laboratories. Nvidia cut off about half of its Asian buyers last July, seemingly in the purview of the export controls, and told data center operators that over 50% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. Meanwhile, both Malaysia and Singapore have intensified their scrutiny of AI hardware shipments. China's countermeasures ammo is as of yet unspecified. The nation had restricted the sale of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the U.S. previously, and the truce shelved that bullet until Nov. 2027. Beijing may well choose to simply not renew that agreement when that day comes. Although analysts believe that the nations will be cordial enough during this summit, Trump's perceived provocation may bring China's proverbial nuclear option of restricting rare earth exports back to the loading bay. The truce on that particular matter only has a few weeks left, expiring on Jan. 10, 2027. Likewise, super-hard materials and high-density lithium batteries, crucial for the newest generations of EVs, solar power storage, and battery installations, all have white flags that will come down early next year. Analysts also expect that Chinese firms and their government will continue to heavily invest in domestic chip production, namely, but not only, by Huawei. Broadly speaking, the U.S.' updated chip control regulation means that Chinese firms cannot sidestep the existing control on chip sales by renting them instead, closing one of the main existing loopholes around the export restrictions. Additionally, selling chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil now also requires a license, as the U.S. Department of Commerce suspects that companies in these nations import Blackwell cards to sell to China.

特朗普与习近平和普京的历史性会晤成为亚洲之行的头条新闻海峡时报
特朗普与习近平和普京的历史性会晤成为亚洲之行的头条新闻
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发表于 2026 年 11 月 19 日 07:05
更新于 2026 年 11 月 19 日 07:25
中国深圳11月19日 - 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将于周四与中国和俄罗斯总统习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京举行史无前例的会晤，以此结束他的亚洲之行，尽管北京方面拒绝将这一问题作为会议的核心议题，但他强调了他的核军控野心。
分析人士表示，三边会议将汇集世界三大核大国的领导人，举行一次不寻常的外交聚会，这可能会展示他们的影响力，但不太可能达成重大协议。
在周三的讲话中，习近平呼吁“自由开放的贸易”，将北京描绘成全球舞台上的稳定伙伴，并与特朗普领导下提高关税并采取更强硬外交政策的美国形成鲜明对比。
后来他在深圳机场迎接特朗普，这是中国领导人的一个不同寻常的举动，但也是对美国总统九月在安德鲁斯联合基地与特朗普上次会面时所提供的礼节的回应。两国领导人还交换了短暂的拥抱。
特朗普和普京上次于 2025 年在阿拉斯加会面，进行会谈，但未能结束俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争。两人在深圳拍照时短暂握手并说了几句话，两人分别站在习近平的两侧。俄罗斯国际文传电讯社称，特朗普和普京没有进行实质性对话。
尽管中国一再反对与拥有更大核武库的华盛顿和莫斯科进行谈判，但特朗普坚持将核军控作为三边会议的核心议题。这种分歧可能会使习近平主持的会议变得复杂，但会议在一定程度上是由特朗普的要求决定的。
特朗普将在三边会议之前与习近平举行双边会议并共进工作午餐，美国和俄罗斯官员表示，他还将与普京进行一对一会晤。俄罗斯官员表示，这次会议没有计划进行全面的双边谈判。
特朗普的特使加大了外交努力，以结束俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争，欧洲领导人也将参与讨论，重点关注战后安全保障和经济复苏规划。
特朗普的亚洲之行提供了一个展示美国影响力、加强与地区盟友关系以及寻求与习近平和普京进行高调外交开放的机会。
但美国总统回国后将面临政治和政策挑战，包括中期选举的影响、英伟达芯片争议以及一系列备受瞩目的技术和航空旅行中断，这些都让美国人感到不安。
保卫民主基金会的克雷格·辛格尔顿表示，三位领导人有充分理由齐聚一堂，但鉴于他们在乌克兰、伊朗、核武器、贸易和中国军力建设方面存在分歧，在实质内容上达成一致的理由要少得多。
辛格尔顿说：“一张照片可以让三个人都受益匪浅。”他补充说，他认为“议程更难达成一致”。
白宫官员表示，预计特朗普不会在三边会议期间提出乌克兰战争问题。然而，特朗普表示他可以提出这个问题，这给领导人之间的冲突是否会进入讨论留下了一些不确定性。
此次聚会也正值盛大的

SHENZHEN, China, Nov 19 - US President Donald Trump will cap his Asia trip on Thursday with an unprecedented meeting with Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, pressing his ambitions for nuclear arms control even as Beijing resists making the issue a centerpiece of the gathering.
The trilateral meeting will bring together the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers for an unusual diplomatic gathering that could showcase their influence but is unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say.
In a speech on Wednesday, Xi called for "free and open trade," portraying Beijing as a stable partner on the global stage, and drawing a contrast with the US, which has raised tariffs and adopted a more muscular foreign policy under Trump.
He later greeted Trump at the airport in Shenzhen, an unusual gesture by the Chinese leader, but one that reciprocated formalities extended by the US president at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met. The leaders also exchanged a brief hug.
Trump and Putin, who last met in Alaska in 2025 for talks that failed to end Russia's war in Ukraine, shared a brief handshake and a few words at a photo opportunity in Shenzhen, where they were placed on either side of Xi. Russia's Interfax news agency said Trump and Putin did not have a substantive conversation.
Trump has insisted nuclear arms control be a central topic of the trilateral, despite China's repeated objections to joining negotiations with Washington and Moscow, which possess far larger nuclear arsenals. The disagreement threatens to complicate a meeting hosted by Xi but shaped in part by Trump's demands.
Trump is to have a bilateral meeting and a working lunch with Xi ahead of the trilateral, and US and Russian officials said he would also have a one-on-one meeting with Putin. The Russian officials said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned at that meeting.
Trump's envoys have intensified diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine, with discussions that are also set to involve European leaders focused on postwar security guarantees and economic recovery planning.
Trump's Asia trip has offered a chance to showcase US influence, strengthen ties with regional allies and pursue a high-profile diplomatic opening with Xi and Putin.
But the US president will return home facing political and policy challenges, including the fallout from bruising midterm elections, the Nvidia chip controversy and a spate of high-profile technology and air travel outages that have rattled Americans.
Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies said the three leaders have plenty of reasons to appear together but far fewer to agree on substance, given their differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons, trade and China's military buildup.
"A photograph could serve all three men well," Singleton said, adding that he thought the "agenda is much harder to agree on."
White House officials have said Trump is not expected to raise the war in Ukraine during the trilateral. Trump, however, has suggested he could bring it up, leaving some uncertainty about whether the conflict will enter discussions among the leaders.
The gathering also comes amid growing tensions over reports of Nvidia chips being diverted to China through Southeast Asia, raising questions about the effectiveness of US export restrictions and the future of Chinese access to advanced technology.
"This is Beijing's worst nightmare. China wants chip access that it can negotiate with the president. It may get chip restrictions written into law by both parties," Singleton said.
Trump's bilateral meeting with Xi on Thursday will also provide an opportunity to assess the durability of a trade truce reached earlier this month.
The president has also expressed interest in meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but US officials have repeatedly said no such encounter is planned during this trip.
Randy Schriver, a former senior Pentagon official in Trump's first administration, said the president would relish such a meeting.
"I think President Trump would meet with Kim Jong Un tomorrow if he could ... he likes the theater, the political theater, the spectacle of it," Schriver said.
Following the trilateral, Trump is scheduled to depart Shenzhen for Washington, concluding a trip that has included regional security and trade engagements in the Philippines and China. REUTERS

美国空军正在加强在该国最西端岛屿的训练，寻求开发更多的地方来投射力量并监视太平洋和北极的对手。这些努力在十月下旬就可见一斑，当时空军部署到阿拉斯加阿留申群岛的谢米亚岛进行一次罕见的演习，空军发布了一份概述其在关岛附近岛屿行动计划的提案。谢米亚距离俄罗斯比阿拉斯加大陆更近，10 月 18 日至 26 日期间，F-16、加油机和货机部署到厄里克森机场。在那里，这些喷气式飞机“保持警惕”，机组人员就位，随时准备在接到通知后立即起飞。阿拉斯加 NORAD 地区发言人 Kitsana Dounglomchan 上尉在一封电子邮件中表示：“虽然飞机在 20 世纪 80 年代处于警戒状态是很常见的事情，但这次部署标志着数十年来飞机在厄尔克森首次处于警戒状态。”作为美国-加拿大国土防御演习的一部分，谢米亚部署以远程行动结束。当 F-16 战机从厄尔克森起飞，覆盖阿拉斯加战区南部时，位于西边 1,600 英里的艾尔森空军基地的 F-35 和 F-16 战机也起飞，覆盖战区西北部。加拿大 CF-18 飞机从距谢米亚 2,600 英里的冷湖基地起飞，覆盖北部地区。
阿拉斯加北美防空司令部司令、空军中将罗伯特·戴维斯在一份新闻稿中表示，从厄尔克森出发的行动“证明我们可以部署到严峻的地点，保持警戒，在短时间内发射，并无缝整合美国和加拿大军队以保卫北方通道”。自二战以来，美国军方一直在谢米亚地区活跃。冷战期间，该基地驻有加油机和侦察机以及雷达，以监视苏联的活动，特别是苏联的洲际弹道导弹。大型 Cobra Dane 雷达建于 20 世纪 70 年代，至今仍用于监测导弹活动。最近在谢米亚的部署突显了其作为阿留申群岛栖息地的持续重要性，阿留申群岛横跨连接太平洋和北极的战略重要水域。 2024 年 9 月，美国士兵使用 HIMARS 发射器进行了一次“兵力投送行动”，此前俄罗斯和中国在该地区进行了一系列活动，其中包括中俄轰炸机在阿拉斯加附近进行的首次巡逻。最近的其他演习似乎侧重于保护该岛的基础设施免受海上入侵和空袭。据一份新闻稿称，在厄里克森期间，飞行员还认证了该基地的飞机拦截系统，可以处理 F-16 战斗机，“进一步验证了厄里克森机场作为未来战斗机在严峻机场执行任务的可行地点”。
Dounglomchan拒绝就厄尔克森的未来行动发表评论，但表示北美防空司令部保持着“作战能力”，可以“在我们选择的时间和地点”在阿拉斯加和北极周围调动部队，并且“经常到厄尔克森这样的偏远地区”。随着谢米亚演习的结束，空军分享了未来在太平洋中部岛屿上的行动计划。 在 10 月底发布的一份提案中，空军表示将研究每年在北马里亚纳群岛联邦罗塔岛、塞班岛和天宁岛的机场进行多达 1,500 次甚至可能超过 1,800 次飞机行动（例如起飞和降落）的影响。这些作业将是小型、中型和大型演习的一部分

The U.S. Air Force is stepping up its training on the country’s westernmost islands as it seeks to develop more places from which to project power and monitor adversaries across the Pacific and the Arctic. Those efforts were visible in late October, when airmen deployed to Shemya Island in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands for a rare exercise, and when the Air Force released a proposal outlining its plans for operations on islands near Guam. On Shemya, which is closer to Russia than to mainland Alaska , F-16s, tankers and cargo planes deployed to Eareckson Air Station from Oct. 18 to Oct. 26. While there, the jets “sat alert,” with crews in position and maintaining readiness to launch on short notice. “While it was commonplace for aircraft to sit alert in the 1980s, this deployment marks the first time in decades that aircraft have sat alert at Eareckson,” Capt. Kitsana Dounglomchan, Alaskan NORAD Region spokesperson, said in an email. The Shemya deployment ended with long-range operations as part of a U.S.-Canada homeland-defense exercise. As F-16s launched from Eareckson to cover the southern portion of the Alaska theater of operations, F-35s and F-16s at Eielson Air Force Base 1,600 miles to the west took off to cover the northwest portion of the theater. Canadian CF-18s flew from their base at Cold Lake, 2,600 miles from Shemya, to cover the northern part. Operating from Eareckson “proved we can deploy to an austere location, maintain alert, launch on short notice, and seamlessly integrate U.S. and Canadian forces to defend the northern approaches,” Air Force Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of the Alaskan NORAD region, said in a press release. The U.S. military has been active on Shemya since World War II. During the Cold War, the base hosted refueling and surveillance aircraft as well as radars to monitor Soviet activity, especially Soviet ICBMs. The massive Cobra Dane radar was built there in the 1970s and is still used to monitor missile activity. Recent deployments to Shemya underscore its continued relevance as a perch in the Aleutians, which stretch across strategically important waters linking the Pacific and Arctic. A “ force projection operation ” by U.S. soldiers with HIMARS launchers in September 2024 came after a flurry of Russian and Chinese activity in the area, including the first Sino-Russian bomber patrol near Alaska. Other recent exercises appear to have focused on defending the island’s infrastructure from seaborne incursions and aerial attacks. While at Eareckson, airmen also certified the base’s aircraft-arresting system to handle F-16s, “further validating Eareckson Air Station as a viable location for future fighter operations from an austere airfield,” according to a press release. Dounglomchan declined to comment on future operations at Eareckson but said NORAD maintains “the operational capability” to move forces around Alaska and the Arctic “at a time and place of our choosing” and “oftentimes to remote locations like Eareckson.” As the drills on Shemya wrapped up, the Air Force shared its plans for future operations on islands in the central Pacific. In a proposal released at the end of October, the service said it would study the impact of conducting up to 1,500 and potentially more than 1,800 aircraft operations, such as takeoffs and landings, annually at airfields on Rota, Saipan, and Tinian in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The operations would be part of small, medium and large drills held several times a year for a few weeks at a time. They would also involve deployment of up to 550,000 gallons of fuel and up to 1,000 personnel at each airfield, as well as munitions, temporary infrastructure, and support operations. The Air Force said its study would assess “the potential social, economic, and environmental effects” of those operations. HC-130J Combat King II pilots assigned to the 211th Rescue Squadron pilot an aircraft en route from Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson to Eareckson Air Station, Alaska, on Oct. 19, 2026. (Airman 1st Class Frank Houseton/U.S. Air Force) The study won’t be completed until mid-2028, but the proposal highlights the Air Force’s recent focus on those islands, especially Tinian, where airmen are refurbishing North Field , one of the U.S.’s largest and most important WWII airbases. North Field was abandoned and overgrown after the war, but airmen have been clearing vegetation, removing debris and rehabilitating runways since late 2023. That work is ongoing but had progressed enough by mid-2025 for North Field to be deemed “a semi-permanent [contingency] location” for the Air Force’s main base on Guam, about 100 miles to the south. The Northern Marianas is a U.S. territory in the Second Island Chain, which stretches from Japan through the central Pacific to Indonesia. The Air Force has been scouting airfields in that island chain and conducting renovations and upgrades to make them better able to support its Agile Combat Employment concept, which emphasizes dispersal and resilience to counter the threat from China. “China’s missile force is large, but it’s not unlimited. Every additional airfield from where the Air Force can operate is another of targets China has to cover. That’s the logic behind Agile Combat Employment,” said Kelly Greico, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center. Improvements on Shemya and in the Northern Marianas enhance the Air Force’s ability to operate in those places, but those operations are influenced by the islands’ locations, according to Greico, whose research focuses on airpower strategy. Shemya “is primarily about homeland defense. Its location in the North Pacific makes it useful mainly as a forward operating location for NORAD,” Greico said. “The value of the remote airfield lies less in its ability to generate sorties under contested conditions than in its geographic position in intercepting Russian aircraft forward.” But investments in Rota, Tinian, and Saipan, Greico added, “are primarily about expanding the number of locations from which the Air Force could operate, reducing its dependence on Andersen Air Base at Guam.” Both Shemya and the Northern Marianas provide the benefit of being U.S. territory, giving the Pentagon greater freedom to operate. Bases in the Philippines and Japan are closer to China, but those countries have more control over what U.S. forces do at their facilities and may limit their access and operations during a crisis or conflict. Geography tempers those political benefits, however. In the Stimson Center’s modeling , dispersal had “the biggest effect of any countermeasure we tested,” Greico said. “But the effect is much smaller in the Second Island Chain than in Japan, because there just aren’t many runways out there.” “Chinese missile strikes could keep U.S. runways in Guam and other Pacific islands closed to tankers and bombers for about four days. Adding civilian airfields in Guam, the Northern Marianas, and Palau only reduced those times by a matter of hours,” Greico added. “Geography matters here. There’s a lot of water out there, but not much land.”

summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《防务一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

SECURING HISTORIC DEALS WITH THE PHILIPPINES: President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. hosted President Trump for a historic State Visit in Manila, where the two leaders announced landmark deals that will strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance and support American companies and workers. The leaders also committed to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines through increased Philippine imports of American energy and agriculture products, which will support the jobs of tens of thousands of American engineers, technicians, and farmers. U.S. companies Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts with GE Aerospace engines, supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs. President Trump’s America First Arms Transfer Strategy ensures that the surge in allies’ spending benefits the U.S. defense industry, reindustrializing America and supporting American jobs while arming our partners with the best capabilities in the world. The United States will utilize $400 million in FMF for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines agreed to partner on supply the Philippines’ sovereign cloud infrastructure with trusted U.S. Super Intelligence technology through the United States’ SI Exports Program. The Philippine Department of National Defense (DND) announced a $37 million contract with a U.S. firm, supporting 140 American jobs. The contract delivers SI-enabled mission support, expands U.S.-Philippine defense cooperation, and improves interoperability. The Philippine DND committed to work with trusted U.S. technology providers on a $63 million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for SI use cases, supporting over 200 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines committed to improving cooperation in critical technologies. The United States and the Philippines announced exploration of an intergovernmental agreement on civil-nuclear technology which would open opportunities for U.S. nuclear companies, support American jobs, and generate gigawatts of energy for the Philippines. This marks the first U.S. civil-nuclear intergovernmental agreement with an Indo-Pacific partner. U.S. company Astranis announced it is offering connectivity services from its U.S.-manufactured AGILA satellite to the Philippines, a commercial opportunity worth up to $200 million, supporting 600 American jobs, to provide independent and secure communications infrastructure for the Philippine government and people. President Trump is leveraging strategic infrastructure to strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, secure critical supply chains, open new markets for American businesses, and support American workers. Subic Grain will build a new $40 million fuel storage depot at Subic Bay to support U.S. military and commercial operations. The United States and the Philippines announced that the Philippines will modernize its Basco Airport to improve U.S.-Philippine operational access, disaster response, and commercial supply chains in the Philippines’ northernmost islands. FINALIZING THE U.S.-THAILAND TRADE DEAL AND INCREASING MILITARY SALES:   At the ASEAN Summit, President Trump announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal and a weapons sale with Thailand that will give American workers, manufacturers, farmers, ranchers, and businesses unprecedented access to Thailand’s market.   The trade deal, once signed, will eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, increasing market access for a full range of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports. The trade deal will also protect and enforce U.S. intellectual property, increase economic security alignment, and strengthen and enforce Thai labor and environmental laws to balance trade. Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS). The sale would give America’s treaty Ally long-range precision fires and support 400 American jobs and the U.S. defense industrial base. Once concluded, it would be the first deal of its kind in mainland Southeast Asia. SECURING INVESTMENT DEALS ACROSS SOUTHEAST ASIA:   President Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for U.S. companies, furthering U.S. leadership in digital connectivity across the region. In Indonesia, U.S. company Latitude Energy and Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced negotiations on a $2 billion project that will use world-class U.S. technology to improve Indonesia’s utilization of its coal resources. Panasonic signed a multi-year agreement to buy advanced silicon-carbon anode materials from U.S. company Sila. The agreement is worth up to $1 billion and will support an additional 500 American jobs. In Malaysia, Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) signed a three-year $100 million agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services, the fuel procurement subsidiary of Malaysia’s national power utility, Tenaga Nasional Berhad. LEADING THE REGION IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE: In addition to Philippine commitments on American SI technology above, President Trump announced further deployment of American SI technology across the region through our SI Exports Program, cementing U.S. firms and American technology as the global standard for trusted partners. President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar announced that a U.S. consortium will develop a sovereign SI cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK. Brunei’s Unified National Networks intends to award U.S. company Vertiv the Rimba Data Centre tender and source the nearly $1 billion buildout from U.S. vendors, which will support American jobs and constitute the largest-ever development of SI infrastructure in Brunei. 11月18日，国家主席习近平在深圳出席亚太经合组织峰会嘉宾欢迎宴会上会见日本首相高市早苗。

习近平在深圳举行的亚太经合组织宴会上与日本首相高市早苗握手，这是自日本首相高市早苗因台湾言论导致两国关系恶化以来的首次正式接触。
日本曾寻求保证习近平不会冷落高市，但她在机场受到的欢迎规模比韩国领导人要小，而且迎接她的是一位前官员。
高一表示台湾的袭击可能威胁日本的生存后，中国和日本的关系仍然紧张。中国要求撤回并实施稀土出口限制。
深圳 — 11 月 18 日，中国国家主席习近平与来访的日本首相高市早苗握手，这是自 2025 年末高市发表涉台言论导致双边关系恶化以来两国领导人的首次正式互动。
此次会面正值习近平和夫人彭丽媛在深圳为出席亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人会议的客人举行的欢迎宴会上接待客人。高一与习近平握手并交谈。高一随后与彭一一握手。
习近平还向其他领导人致意并合影留念。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京站在习近平和彭丽媛的左边，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普紧邻他们的右边。高市位于后排，距离中间好几个位置。
彭博新闻社 11 月初报道称，日本官员已向中国寻求保证，表示习近平将在峰会上给予高市与其他世界领导人相同的待遇，并避免日本领导人受到冷落。
尽管在欢迎宴会上有互动，但当高一当天早些时候抵达深圳机场时，接待她的是一位前中国外交部官员，而不是现任官员。与当天早些时候韩国总统李在明的欢迎仪式相比，规模要小得多。
日本外务省新闻秘书北村敏博在会见记者时淡化了高一与习近平握手的重要性，称其为“正常礼节”。
高市于 2025 年 11 月向国会表示，中国对台湾的攻击可能构成威胁日本生存的局面，此后中日关系急剧恶化。尽管东京长期以来一直持有这种观点，但历届首相都避免公开表达这一观点，以防止与北京的关系出现恶化。
中国声称对台湾实行民主治理，是其领土的一部分，对此作出愤怒反应，并要求高市收回言论。她没有这样做。日本坚称与中国沟通的大门仍然敞开，但过去一年东京和北京之间的高层互动很少。
中国对日本实施了一系列政治和经济措施，包括限制对日本汽车和科技行业至关重要的稀土出口。中国还指责高市奉行“新军国主义”，因为她寻求增加对日本防务部门的投资。

China’s Xi shakes hands with Takaichi as ties remain strained

Xi Jinping shook hands with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the APEC banquet in Shenzhen, their first official contact since ties worsened over her Taiwan comments.
Japan had sought reassurance that Xi would not snub Takaichi, but her airport welcome was smaller than South Korea’s leader and she was met by a former official.
China and Japan remain tense after Takaichi said a Taiwan attack could threaten Japan’s survival. China has demanded a retraction and imposed rare-earth export curbs.
SHENZHEN – Chinese President Xi Jinping shook hands with visiting Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Nov 18, the first official interaction between the two leaders since bilateral ties deteriorated late in 2025 in the wake of comments made by Takaichi about Taiwan.
The encounter came as Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, received guests at a welcome banquet for guests attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen. Takaichi shook hands with Xi, after which they exchanged a few words. Takaichi then shook hands with Peng.
Xi also greeted other leaders and posed with them for a group photo. Russian President Vladimir Putin stood to the left of Xi and Peng, with US President Donald Trump immediately to their right. Takaichi was several places from the centre in the back row.
Bloomberg News reported earlier in November that Japanese officials had sought reassurances from China that Xi would give Takaichi the same treatment as other world leaders at the summit and avoid a snub of the Japanese leader.
Despite the interaction at the welcome banquet, when Takaichi arrived at Shenzhen airport earlier in the day she was received by a former Chinese Foreign Ministry official rather than a current official. The welcome ceremony was much smaller than that for South Korean President Lee Jae Myung earlier in the day.
At a meeting with journalists, Japanese Foreign Ministry press secretary Toshihiro Kitamura played down the significance of Takaichi’s handshake with Xi, describing it as “normal protocol”.
Relations between China and Japan deteriorated sharply after Takaichi told parliament in November 2025 that a Chinese attack on Taiwan could constitute a situation threatening Japan’s survival. While that has long been the view in Tokyo, previous prime ministers have avoided stating it in public to prevent roiling ties with Beijing.
China, which claims democratically governed Taiwan as part of its territory, reacted angrily and demanded that Takaichi retract the remarks. She has not done so. Japan has insisted that the door to communication with China remains open, but there has been minimal high-level interaction between Tokyo and Beijing in the past year.
China has imposed a series of political and economic measures against Japan, including restrictions on rare-earth exports that are important to the Japanese auto and technology industries. China has also accused Takaichi of “neo-militarism” as she seeks to increase investment in Japan’s defence sector.
On Nov 18, Takaichi greeted Chinese Minister of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Zhang Zhu before they sat down for an ASEAN meeting with China, Japan and South Korea. BLOOMBERG

维也纳 — — 联合国核监察机构负责人拉斐尔·格罗西 (Rafael Grossi) 11 月 18 日表示，随着朝鲜继续扩大武器级材料的生产，朝鲜已对其宁边核设施的原铀浓缩工厂进行了扩建。
自平壤于 2009 年驱逐核查人员以来，国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 一直无法进入朝鲜。该机构目前主要使用卫星图像来观察该国。
朝鲜，正式名称为朝鲜民主主义人民共和国（DPRK），已经进行了多次核试验，并且似乎继续生产两种可用于制造核武器核心的材料——高浓缩铀和钚。
格罗西在向国际原子能机构 35 国理事会季度会议发表的一份声明中表示：“此前，我已向大家报告了江山和宁边浓缩设施的持续运行情况、宁边增建浓缩设施的情况，以及据报道朝鲜进一步扩大武器级核材料生产的情况。”
康村位于平壤西南部，而宁边更大的遗址则距离首都更远。
他表示：“自 2026 年 9 月中旬以来，原宁边浓缩设施的进一步扩建工程一直在建设中，新的扩建工程将于 2026 年 10 月下旬在外部完成。”但他没有详细说明。
“朝鲜不断扩大的铀浓缩计划仍然令人严重关切，”他补充道。
格罗西表示，国际原子能机构还“观察到迹象”，朝鲜用来从乏燃料生产钚的宁边5兆瓦核反应堆可能仍在继续运行，并处于第七个辐照周期，之后乏燃料将被移走进行后处理。
他补充说，宁边的另一个轻水反应堆自四月份以来一直在运行。路透社

Published Nov 18, 2026, 09:40 PM

VIENNA – North Korea has built an extension to its original uranium-enrichment plant at its Yongbyon nuclear complex as it continues to expand its production of weapons-grade material, UN nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Nov 18.
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009. The agency now observes the country using mainly satellite imagery.
North Korea, formally known as the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), has carried out several nuclear tests and appears to continue to produce the two materials with which one can make the core of a nuclear weapon – highly enriched uranium and plutonium.
“Previously, I have reported to you about the ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Kangson and Yongbyon, the construction of an additional enrichment facility at Yongbyon, and the reported further expansion of the DPRK’s production of weapons-grade nuclear material,” Grossi said in a statement to a quarterly meeting of the IAEA’s 35-nation board of governors.
Kangson is just outside Pyongyang to the south-west, while the much larger site at Yongbyon is further away from the capital to the north.
“Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction, with the new extension externally complete by late October 2026,” he said, without elaborating.
“The ongoing expansion of the DPRK’s uranium enrichment programme remains a cause for serious concern,” he added.
Grossi said the IAEA has also “observed indications” that the 5-megawatt nuclear reactor at Yongbyon that North Korea uses to produce plutonium from spent fuel probably continues to operate and is in its seventh irradiation cycle, after which the spent fuel would be removed for reprocessing.
Another light-water reactor in Yongbyon has been operating since April, he added. REUTERS

content:
2026年11月18日，在廣東省深圳市舉行的亞太經合組織（APEC）峰會歡迎晚宴前，美國總統川普（左）與俄羅斯總統普京握手。(Lori Sagisawa/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月19日訊】（大紀元記者張婷綜合報導）美國總統川普（特朗普）週三（11月18日）抵達中國深圳，開啟了他亞洲之行中最關鍵的一環：與中共黨魁習近平及俄羅斯總統普京舉行一場史無前例的三邊峰會。在川普積極斡旋俄烏戰爭和平協議以及普京面臨西方孤立之際，兩人之間的互動倍受國際關注。
路透社報導，世界領導人聚集在一起，握手自是常態，但週三發生的一次握手格外引人注目：普京和川普的握手意味深長。
在參加APEC峰會期間拍集體照時，普京走向川普，距離還有一段就伸出了手，一直走到跟前，兩人熱情握手。川普還拍了拍普京。在俄羅斯因入侵烏克蘭而遭到西方大部分國家孤立的背景下，這一舉動公開展示了兩人之間的親善姿態。（點擊這裡看相關視頻。）
路透社分析認為，這一幕讓普京有機會向外界展示，他仍能與美國總統直接接觸，在國際舞台上仍有一席之地。對川普而言，這一互動則體現出他重視與其他世界領導人建立私人關係。
雖然這次短暫互動不能保證在政策上取得任何突破，但為週四（11月19日）的會晤營造了友好氣氛。屆時，川普、普京和習近平將舉行首次三邊會晤。預計川普還將與普京單獨會面。
川普希望在三邊會晤中討論限制核武器問題。他還表示，烏克蘭和伊朗問題也將被納入討論範疇。
據美國全國廣播公司（NBC）報導，華盛頓智庫保衛民主基金會（Foundation for Defense of Democracies）中國問題專家克雷格‧辛格爾頓（Craig Singleton）表示，川普寄望於憑藉私人關係，將各國領導人召集到一起談論這一問題，這是其他美國總統無法做到的。
川普週二（11月17日）在菲律賓參加東盟—美國特別峰會期間，也強調了建立私人關係的重要性。他當時對在座的東盟國家領導人說，彼此熟識真的會讓事情順利得多。他說，自己幾乎了解在座的所有人，這讓雙方合作起來容易得多，也順暢得多。
